about: Backend engineer with 8 years of experience in commercial development — the last 4 years in Java backend for banking and insurance, and 4 years before that in C++/C# building a static code analyzer used to catch bugs and vulnerabilities in production codebases. Comfortable stepping into temporary team lead duties: planning releases, splitting up work across a 7-person team, and making sure things ship.
Current stack: Java 21, virtual threads, Spring Boot / Cloud / Data, Hibernate, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, Resilience4j.

experience.summary: One of Russia's largest privately-owned banks (10M+ retail clients). Backend for a mobile insurance app — microservices handling policy issuance, payment, and pension fund flows.
bullets: Fixed a race condition in policy issuance/payment by moving the flow to a transactional inbox pattern (Kafka–PostgreSQL) — eliminated issuance errors and simplified incident debugging
Fixed a DB connection-pool exhaustion causing wide API degradation on the core insurance service — narrowed transaction scope, cutting latency by ~85–90%
Built the endpoint behind a main-screen product widget — highest-traffic call in our API at 1.3M requests/day, ~35 req/s at peak — using Resilience4j and Redis caching for latency and resilience
Own release prep and deployment end-to-end: build, packaging, rollout via Kubernetes and ArgoCD/GitLab CI
Design and stand up new microservices from scratch, including security review sign-off
Covered as team lead during absence — planned releases, prioritized work across a 7-person team (2 devs, 3 analysts, 2 QA)
Run team retros and a technical book club (Kafka, Designing Data-Intensive Applications)
Built a prototype toxic-comment moderation service using DJL for BERT inference, with MinIO/S3 storage
Write unit/integration tests (JUnit, Mockito, Testcontainers, WireMock), review code, join incident postmortems, resolve infosec findings

experience.summary: Intermediary banking service aggregating data across integrations and checking loan offers for business customers, built for one of the top banks in Russia.
bullets: Built a health-monitoring service for the aggregator and its dependent microservices
Took part in architecture decisions and service design; built REST APIs and integrations with adjacent microservices
Covered the codebase with unit and integration tests (JUnit, Mockito, Testcontainers)
Set up technical documentation practices for the project from scratch
Wrote a 200+ page Java reference guide for onboarding junior developers; gave an internal talk on Spring Cloud
experience.stack: Stack: Java 17, PostgreSQL, MyBatis, Liquibase, Kafka, OpenShift

experience.summary: Back-office gateway processing thousands of payment documents, enriching and validating them against current legislation. Used in 2 of the top-10 banks in Russia.
bullets: Kept the codebase backward-compatible with Java 6 for clients on older platform versions
Refactored and developed payment document processing logic, with test coverage
Fixed issues surfaced by static code analysis
Set up technical documentation that significantly cut onboarding time for new hires

Developed an internal CRM system (Blazor + PostgreSQL); owned the backend mail-generation system, migrated the statistics report system to the new CRM, and converted data from the old CRM database (MySQL → PostgreSQL)
Developed internal CusDev automation services — one decision increased customer retention by 30%
Designed and implemented a reports generation system pulling from Bitbucket/YouTrack, CRM, SVN, and Jenkins to support business decisions, incorporating management and stakeholder feedback
Joined client calls and mentored new hires

positions.summary: PVS-Studio is a static analyzer for code quality, security (SAST), and code safety.
bullets: Developed and supported general-purpose and MISRA-based diagnostic rules for the static analyzer
Conducted algorithmic research for analyzer optimization
Wrote marketing articles targeted at developers
